calls.head: Sorokin doesn’t own the Oilers
calls.body: Sorokin has been a wall against the Oilers since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Sorokin isn’t that wall tonight.
calls.call: If Sorokin starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .906 than to his .943 against the Oilers.

calls.head: Penalties could cost the Islanders
calls.body: The Islanders’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Oilers’ power play is the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Islanders tonight. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

calls.head: Depth vs. Star power
calls.body: The Islanders roll four lines, but the Oilers lean on their top six. The Islanders are one of the league’s best for depth, and Edmonton is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.

surprises.head: A shutout for Tristan Jarry
surprises.body: Jarry stopped all 18 shots, worth 2.1 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 15 starts.

story.head: Jarry blanks the Islanders
paras: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Vasily Podkolzin scored just over a minute apart midway through the second to put the Oilers up 2-0. Nugent-Hopkins struck again on the power play late in the period to make it 3-0. Jason Dickinson added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 4-0.
The Oilers had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Islanders 24-18. Tristan Jarry turned aside all 18 shots for the Oil, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 20 of 23 at the other end.

Emil Heineman was thrown out with a game misconduct early in the first. Scott Mayfield picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Oilers killed all four Islanders power plays. The Oilers moved to 10-2-2, still first in the Pacific, while the Islanders dropped to 7-5-2, fourth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Connor McDavid has a point in every game this season.
Matthew Schaefer’s six-game point streak ended.
Jason Dickinson scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 12 (17 games played since).

The Islanders were without Mathew Barzal, Matias Maccelli, Alexander Romanov and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team was missing more at the time.
